import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 978

*Reference:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/978](https://www.erdosproblems.com/978)
 - [Ho67] Hooley, C., On the power free values of polynomials. Mathematika (1967), 21--26.
 - [Br11] Browning, T. D., Power-free values of polynomials. Arch. Math. (Basel) (2011), 139--150.
 - [Er53] Erdős, P., Arithmetical properties of polynomials. J. London Math. Soc. (1953), 416--425.
-/

open Polynomial Set

namespace Erdos978

/-- Let `f ∈ ℤ[X]` be an irreducible polynomial with positive leading coefficient. Suppose that the
degree `k` of `f` is larger than `2` and is not equal to a power of `2`. Then the set of `n` such
that `f n` is `(k - 1)`-th power free is infinite, and this is proved in [Er53]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_978.variants.sub_one {f : ℤ[X]} (hi : Irreducible f) (hd : 2 < f.natDegree)
    (hp : ∀ (x : ℕ), f.natDegree ≠ 2 ^ x) (hlc : 0 < f.leadingCoeff) :
    {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 1) (f.eval (n : ℤ))}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/-- Let `f ∈ ℤ[X]` be an irreducible polynomial with positive leading coefficient. Suppose that the
degree `k` of `f` is larger than `2`, is not equal to a power of `2`, and `f n` has no fixed
`(k - 1)`-th power divisors other than `1`. Then the set of `n` such that `f n` is `(k - 1)`-th
power free has positive density, and this is proved in [Ho67]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_978.parts.i {f : ℤ[X]} (hi : Irreducible f) (hd : 2 < f.natDegree)
    (hp2 : ∀ (x : ℕ), f.natDegree ≠ 2 ^ x) (hlc : 0 < f.leadingCoeff)
    (hp : ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∃ n : ℕ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ^ (f.natDegree - 1) ∣ f.eval (n : ℤ)) :
    HasPosDensity {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 1) (f.eval (n : ℤ))} := by
  sorry

/-- If the degree `k` of `f` is larger than or equal to `9`, then the set of `n` such that `f n` is
`(k - 2)`-th power free has infinitely many elements. This result is proved in [Br11]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_978.variants.sub_two {f : ℤ[X]} (hi : Irreducible f) (hd : 9 ≤ f.natDegree)
    (hp : ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∃ n : ℕ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ^ (f.natDegree - 1) ∣ f.eval (n : ℤ)) :
    {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 2) (f.eval (n : ℤ))}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
If $k > 3$ (and $k \neq 2^l$), then are there infinitely many $n$ for which $f(n)$ is
$(k-2)$-power-free?

This was disproved by the DeepMind prover agent.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
formal_proof using formal_conjectures at "https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/3b5d6ac2555cd63b83d418c29ff040876be9dee0/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/978.lean#L64"]
theorem erdos_978.variants.allow_fixed_divisors : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ {f : ℤ[X]}, Irreducible f → f.natDegree > 3 →
    (¬ ∃ l : ℕ, f.natDegree = 2 ^ l) → 0 < f.leadingCoeff →
    (¬ ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, (p : ℤ) ^ (f.natDegree - 1) ∣ f.eval (n : ℤ)) →
    {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 2) (f.eval (n : ℤ))}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
If $k>3$ (and $k \neq 2^l$), and for all primes $p$ there exists $n$ such that $p^{k-2}\nmid f(n)$,
then are there infinitely many $n$ for which $f(n)$ is $(k-2)$-power-free?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_978.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ {f : ℤ[X]}, Irreducible f → f.natDegree > 3 →
    (¬ ∃ l : ℕ, f.natDegree = 2 ^ l) → 0 < f.leadingCoeff →
    (∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∃ n : ℕ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ^ (f.natDegree - 2) ∣ f.eval (n : ℤ)) →
    {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 2) (f.eval (n : ℤ))}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/-- Does `n ^ 4 + 2` represent infinitely many squarefree numbers? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_978.parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔ {n : ℕ | Squarefree (n ^ 4 + 2)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos978

findings.description: The local obstruction hypothesis `hp` excludes fixed `(f.natDegree - 1)`-st powers, but the conclusion concerns `(f.natDegree - 2)`-power-free values. The former condition is too weak. A counterexample at the smallest permitted degree is f(X) = ∏_{i=0}^8 (X - 3i) + 384. This polynomial is monic and Eisenstein at 3, hence irreducible, with degree 9. Every f(n) is divisible by 2^7, so the set in the conclusion is empty. Nevertheless, f(0) = 384 is not divisible by p^8 for any prime p, satisfying `hp`. The complete counterexample and the negation of the declaration's universally quantified statement were proved without `sorry` in `/workspace/review/counterexample.lean`, theorem `refutes_sub_two`.
findings.source_evidence: Browning [Br11], Theorem 1 and the immediately following paragraph (pp. 1–2 of the author's preprint), states that the density constant vanishes exactly when there is a fixed power divisor, and concludes infinitely many `(d - 2)`-free values for d ≥ 9 only when that obstruction is absent: https://web.archive.org/web/20110401122225id_/http://www.maths.bris.ac.uk/~matdb/preprints/powerfree.pdf . The remarks at https://www.erdosproblems.com/978 explicitly specify that Browning's result assumes no prime p satisfies p^(k-2) ∣ f(n) for every n.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the exponent in `hp` by `f.natDegree - 2`: `(hp : ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∃ n : ℕ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ^ (f.natDegree - 2) ∣ f.eval (n : ℤ))`. Include this necessary hypothesis in the docstring. The corrected result can retain its `research solved` category.

reformulations.difference: Lean adds an explicit hypothesis excluding fixed `(k - 1)`-st prime-power divisors, whereas the source's positive-density question does not state this hypothesis under its degree restrictions.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The additional hypothesis follows from the other assumptions. A nonconstant irreducible polynomial in ℤ[X] is primitive, and every fixed divisor of a primitive degree-k polynomial divides k! (explicitly recalled in Erdős [Er53], §1). For k > 2 not a power of two, v₂(k!) = k - s₂(k) ≤ k - 2. For an odd prime p, v_p(k!) ≤ (k - 1)/(p - 1) < k - 1. Thus no p^(k-1) can divide every value. Adding this condition does not weaken the source's claim.

reformulations.difference: Although this deliberately weaker variant represents the question without the necessary `(k - 2)`-power obstruction hypothesis, Lean still excludes fixed `(k - 1)`-st prime powers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: That remaining restriction is automatic for the permitted irreducible polynomials and degrees: every fixed divisor divides k!, and k! contains no prime to exponent k - 1 when k > 2 is not a power of two. Consequently this is equivalent to the unconditioned variant discussed in the source, not a negative answer to the properly conditioned `parts.ii`. Its negative answer was also independently verified with the degree-nine counterexample in `/workspace/review/counterexample.lean`; the general redundancy equivalence itself was not formalized.

reformulations.difference: Lean counts infinitely many natural-number inputs rather than explicitly counting infinitely many represented squarefree values, and permits n = 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The function n ↦ n^4 + 2 is injective on ℕ, so its image of the squarefree-input set is infinite exactly when the input set is infinite. Removing n = 0 cannot change infinitude. Both the image equivalence and the general positive-input boundary equivalence were proved without `sorry` in `/workspace/review/boundaries.lean`.

review.notes: All six declarations were checked, including the definitions of Powerfree, Squarefree, natural density, and polynomial degree/irreducibility. No other mathematical defect or status discrepancy was found. In particular, `variants.sub_one` does not need an additional fixed-divisor hypothesis under its existing degree restrictions. The three experiment files (`scratch.lean`, `counterexample.lean`, and `boundaries.lean`) compile successfully. The counterexample and the independent verification of `allow_fixed_divisors` depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, not sorryAx or the problem-file assertions. Hooley's full article was inaccessible; its original opening extract, Browning's account of the result, and the Erdős problem page were sufficient to verify `parts.i`. The target file remains identical to its committed version.

submission.summary: Changed the local obstruction hypothesis to exclude fixed (degree − 2)-nd prime powers and documented this necessary condition. All other declarations, references, and attributes were left unchanged. The requested compile command succeeds with only `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
